subject: Tenant warmup surge — ops bridge request and customer coordination
messages:
From: Luis Ramos <luis@edgemarket.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Sudden increase in warmup latency and queued requests

Hi Soojin,

We're seeing a sudden spike in warmup latency for our dedicated pool this morning (queue times jumping from ~20ms to >1.2s per request over a 30-minute window). This is impacting our inference tail latency and causing timeouts in a couple of internal endpoints. Initial look at our side shows heavy fanout from a scheduled batch job that typically ramps slowly, but today it appears to have started all workers simultaneously.

Can Redwood confirm if there were any autoscaler events, eviction waves, or throttling around 08:30–09:00 PST? We're still collecting logs but wanted to get an ops bridge if needed.

Attachments: short snippet of our client-side traces (client-trace-20261120.txt)

Thanks,
Luis Ramos
Head of Platform Engineering
EdgeMarket

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:31:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Sudden increase in warmup latency and queued requests

Bridge notes (preliminary):

- Observed: At 08:28 PST we see a sudden concurrent warmup fanout from tenant EdgeMarket: 220 simultaneous warmup connections targeting the model shard set A. Average warmup token processing spiked and the allocator began queuing creation of new worker pods.
- Autoscaler behavior: The autoscaler triggered scale-up, but a race between pod warmup and request queuing caused sustained tail latency. No eviction events during this window.
- Config anomaly: EdgeMarket's reserved pool has autoscaler min_replicas set to 2 (intended for cost control). That combined with a large cold fanout resulted in repeated slow starts instead of prewarmed standby.

Action taken:
- Temporarily enabled prefix caching for EdgeMarket's tenant and bumped a small warm standby (added 4 warm pods) to drain queued requests — saw tail latency drop back under 150ms within ~7 minutes.
- Collected logs: serving/20261120/edgemarket/*. (zipped and attached as serving-logs-20261120.zip)

Next steps (proposed):
1) Short-term: recommend EdgeMarket increase min_replicas to 6 for heavy scheduled ramps OR schedule staggered worker starts (we can help with rollout script).
2) Mid-term: create a warmup policy for scheduled batch jobs (auto-stagger + prewarmed slots).
3) Postmortem: publish root cause and compensation plan.

I'll attach the autoscaler config snippets and a runbook draft.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime

Date: 2026-11-21T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Post-incident update: warmup surge mitigation, recommended config changes, and next steps

Hi Luis — quick follow-up with the confirmed timeline and next steps after our bridge yesterday. Thank you and your team for being responsive on logs and traces.

Summary (what happened):
- 08:28 PST 2026-11-20: Large concurrent warmup fanout from EdgeMarket's scheduled batch job caused ~220 simultaneous warmup requests across model shard set A.
- Autoscaler attempted to scale but warm pod init times plus request queuing produced tail latency >1s for ~12 minutes. No GPU evictions were observed.

What we did (remediation):
- Enabled prefix caching and added 4 warm pods; tail latency reduced to <150ms in ~7 minutes.
- Identified autoscaler config (min_replicas=2) as a root contributor to the slow recovery.

Customer-facing recommendations (we can implement alongside you):
1) Temporary guardrail: set min_replicas=6 during scheduled batch windows (we can automate this policy).
2) Implement staggered worker-start script (we will provide a rollout script and review).
3) Add prewarm tokens and prefix caching for high-fanout endpoints.

Commitments from Redwood:
- We will publish a concise postmortem (technical + impact) by 2026-11-24.
- Commercial: Ben will propose a one-time credit covering the affected window; DocuSign link will be provided for formal acknowledgement.
- Ops: Neha will deliver the autoscaler config diff and a recommended runbook snippet by EOD 2026-11-21.

Attachments: serving-logs-20261120.zip, autoscaler-config-snippets.txt, ops-runbook-draft.md

If you agree to the temporary min_replicas change, let us know the first batch window you'd like us to protect and we will schedule a maintenance window or apply as a temporary rule.

Thanks again — we'll be in touch with the postmortem and follow-up items.

Regards,
